urgent.heading: Seek medical advice for new concerns
paragraphs: New or worsening symptoms need appropriate medical advice. Do not assume every change is part of an existing illness or something to work through with exercise.
For severe or life-threatening symptoms, call 000. Otherwise, speak with your GP or treating medical team about symptoms that concern you.

pattern.heading: Tell us what an appointment would need to account for
pattern.intro: An illness does not have to be visible to affect daily activity. Experiences differ, and the details of yours matter when considering care.

items.title: Capacity that varies
items.copy: You may need to explain what is manageable on different days and how you respond after activity.

items.title: The effort of attending
items.copy: Travel and appointments can use energy. Ask about appointment format and any requirements before booking.

items.title: An existing medical plan
items.copy: Bring up relevant diagnoses, restrictions and advice from your treating team.

items.title: A specific movement concern

explainer.heading: What we mean by invisible illnesses
paragraphs: Invisible illness is a broad description for health problems that may not be apparent to other people. It is not one diagnosis, and there is no single exercise or treatment approach that fits everyone included under the term.

Alpha’s role is musculoskeletal assessment and support when appropriate. Diagnosis and treatment of underlying conditions such as ME/CFS, POTS, autoimmune conditions or endometriosis remain with your medical team.

If you have a specific pain or movement concern, we can discuss whether it falls within our scope alongside your existing medical care. A clinic appointment should not replace investigation or advice from your GP or specialist.

focus.heading: Discuss suitability first
paragraphs: Tell reception what you want assessed, who is currently involved in your care and any appointment requirements. Ask whether an appropriate practitioner and format are available.
If an appointment is suitable, explain your concerns and the effects of activity. You can ask about proposed assessment or care, its limits and alternatives before agreeing to it.
Any support needs to account for your medical circumstances and response to activity. Another provider or approach may be more appropriate.

process.heading: Work out whether musculoskeletal support fits

steps.title: Describe your concerns
steps.copy: Explain the particular movement or pain concern and what you hope an assessment would clarify.

steps.title: Share the medical context

steps.title: Consider scope and suitability

steps.copy: Tell the clinician about symptom worsening, including delayed effects. A plan may need changing or stopping.

steps.title: Keep your treating team involved
steps.copy: Discuss communication with other professionals where appropriate and with your consent.

note.heading: General exercise advice may be inappropriate
paragraphs: For people with ME/CFS, symptoms can worsen after exertion. General exercise advice may make symptoms worse, and exercise is not a cure for ME/CFS. Fixed increases in activity or advice to push through symptoms are inappropriate.

The NICE ME/CFS guideline recommends specialist-team oversight for any individual exercise programme that a person chooses to undertake. Musculoskeletal support at Alpha must sit alongside that specialist advice.

If you have ME/CFS or delayed symptom worsening after activity, discuss this with your medical or specialist team before considering exercise advice. This concern must not be treated as ordinary lack of fitness.

faqs.question: Is invisible illness a diagnosis?
faqs.answer: No. It describes health problems that may not be outwardly apparent. Different illnesses have different assessment and care needs; unexplained symptoms should be discussed with an appropriate medical professional.

faqs.question: Does Alpha diagnose the underlying illness?
faqs.answer: Alpha’s role here is musculoskeletal assessment and support. Diagnosis of ME/CFS, POTS, fibromyalgia, autoimmune conditions or other underlying illnesses requires appropriate medical assessment. Discuss diagnosis and medical treatment with your GP or specialist.

faqs.question: Can I enquire while seeing another medical team?
faqs.answer: Yes. Explain the specific concern, your current medical care and any restrictions. We can discuss whether an appropriate musculoskeletal appointment is available. Do not replace existing medical advice with a general exercise plan.

faqs.question: What if activity makes my symptoms worse later?
faqs.answer: Tell your medical or specialist team and any clinician you consult. Delayed worsening after exertion needs particular consideration. For ME/CFS, general exercise advice may worsen symptoms and exercise programmes require specialist oversight; fixed increases or pushing through are inappropriate.

faqs.question: What information might be useful?
faqs.answer: Relevant letters, diagnoses, restrictions or advice from your treating team may help the discussion. Explain how activity affects you and what you want assessed. You do not need to prove how ill you feel with a particular test result.

faqs.question: Can you accommodate my appointment needs?
faqs.answer: Contact reception to discuss what you need, including appointment format or access requirements. Check which arrangements are available before booking.

closing.heading: Ask whether this is the right care for your concern
closing.copy: Call 03 9962 5539 to discuss the concern and your appointment requirements before booking. Your medical team remains central to care for the underlying illness.
